body:
### What are you really trying to do?

I have cancelled a workflow while it is running `await workflow.start_child_workflow()`. The temporal-ui shows "The request to cancel this Workflow Execution has been sent". But the workflow kept running and never cancelled.

### Describe the bug

Events:
```
29 Start Child Workflow Execution Initiated
30 Workflow Execution Cancel Requested
31 Workflow Task Scheduled
32 Child Workflow Execution Started
33 Workflow Task Started
34 Workflow Task Completed
35 Request Cancel External Workflow Execution Initiated
36 Timer Started
37 External Workflow Execution Cancel Requested
38 Workflow Task Scheduled
39 Workflow Task Started
40 Workflow Task Completed
41 Child Workflow Execution Canceled
42 Workflow Task Scheduled
43 Workflow Task Started
44 Workflow Task Completed
45 Timer Fired
...
```

Code
```
@workflow.run
async def run(self, ...):
    ...
    await workflow.start_child_workflow(ReminderWorkflow.run, ...)
    await workflow.sleep(10)
```
And there's a separate application to start the workflow and request cancellation of the workflow.
It is repo'ed many times in our environment.

### Minimal Reproduction

<!-- 
Modify our hello world templates to demonstrate:

- TypeScript: https://github.com/temporalio/samples-typescript/tree/main/hello-world
- Go: https://github.com/temporalio/money-transfer-project-template-go
- Java: https://github.com/temporalio/money-transfer-project-template-java
- PHP: https://github.com/temporalio/samples-php#samples
-->

### Environment/Versions

<!-- Please complete the following information where relevant. -->

- OS and processor: M1 Mac
- Temporal Version: 1.29.1 
- SDK version: PythonSDK 1.25.0
- Are you using Docker or Kubernetes or building Temporal from source?

### Additional context

<!-- Add any other context about the problem here. -->
Check this line: https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python/blob/40e75f660df41f943bc9367b7cdc7a87f4221d19/temporalio/worker/_workflow_instance.py#L2016
It seems the start_child_workflow is shielding from `CancelledError`, which might explain why the cancelled exception is swallowed.

comments.body: Seems like a good bug report. We'll take a look as soon as we can. I think the `shield` is a red herring, because that prevents the _inner_ future from being cancelled, not the outer one. But the `except` around it should probably consider workflow cancellation.

title: [Bug] CancelledError is swallowed during workflow.start_child_workflow
